title: Policy evaluation: decision context walkthrough and explainability log patterns
content:
Purpose
This note walks through a decision-level view of the policy evaluation engine: how a request's decision context is assembled, constraints are evaluated and aggregated, and how lightweight explainability traces should be emitted to support debugging, audits, and downstream model-selection routing. The intent is operational: propose a stable, low-cost log shape that supports forensic analysis and replay without exploding token or storage costs.

Scope and assumptions
- Input: a single inference request (chat or generate) that requires runtime policy checks before selecting a serving model and route.
- Control plane has access to customer tier, region, and configured policy bundles (constraints, fallbacks, cost caps).
- This is not the full policy authoring UX; focus is on runtime evaluation semantics, scoring, and explainability output.

Key concepts and terminology
- Decision context: flattened set of attributes used by rules (customer_id, route, model_family, prompt_tags, geo, SLA_tier, request_size_tokens, cached_prefix_hit, etc.).
- Constraint: boolean predicate (hard) or graded predicate (soft) evaluated against the decision context. Each constraint has an id, type, and cost/latency budget relevance.
- Scorer / aggregator: converts raw constraint outputs into an overall decision score for a route/model candidate.
- Explainability log (x-log): compact record emitted per evaluated candidate that captures provenance for the decision.

Evaluation pipeline (walkthrough)
1) Context enrichment (0.2–1ms):
   - Enrich incoming request with route metadata (route_id, max_latency_ms), customer policy bundle snapshot id, and region affinity hints.
   - Fetch small cache of per-customer overrides (max_model_cost, disabled_models) from local control-plane cache.
2) Candidate expansion (1–5ms):
   - Candidate set is assembled: compatible model versions, quantization variants, and regional replicas. Prefiltering uses capabilities (supports-streaming, supports-functions) + customer allowlist.
3) Constraint evaluation (2–10ms):
   - Evaluate hard constraints first (short-circuit): example hard constraints — data residency, explicit opt-out, malformed request patterns. If any hard constraint fails for a candidate, mark candidate = REJECTED and emit minimal x-log (reason=hard-fail, constraint_ids=[...]).
   - For surviving candidates, evaluate soft constraints: cost_cap, latency_estimate, quality_score_estimate, recency_penalty. Each soft constraint returns a numeric score in [0,1] and an uncertainty band (low, mid, high).
4) Scoring and normalization (1–3ms):
   - Apply configurable weights per constraint group. We follow a two-stage normalization: per-constraint z-like normalization (clamped), then weighted sum -> final candidate_score in [0,100].
   - Apply tie-breakers: prefer local-region candidate if score difference < epsilon, otherwise prefer lower estimated cost.
5) Routing decision and fallback planning (0.5–2ms):
   - Pick top-N candidates. If top candidate is spotty (estimated latency SLO breach probability > p), schedule fallback: immediate next candidate with warm-standby flag.
   - Persist a compact decision fingerprint (policy_bundle_id, evaluation_ts, candidate_ids, decision_hash) to support later audit.

Explainability logs: shape and rationale
- Goals: small, structured, searchable, privacy-safe, replayable. Avoid storing full prompts or user messages.
- Emit an x-log per evaluated candidate with the following flat fields (string or numeric):
  - evaluation_id (UUID)
  - request_id
  - customer_id (hashed)
  - policy_bundle_id
  - candidate_id (model:variant:region)
  - candidate_rank (int)
  - final_score (float)
  - hard_fail_reasons (comma-separated strings or empty)
  - soft_scores (comma-separated ordered floats aligned to documented constraint ids)
  - weight_vector (comma-separated floats)
  - latency_estimate_ms (float)
  - cost_estimate_usd (float)
  - cache_hit (bool)
  - short_circuit_stage (string: prefilter|hard-checks|scoring)
  - decision (string: accept|reject|fallback)
  - decision_ts (ISO date)
  - evaluator_version (string)
  - provenance_tags (comma-separated short tags: e.g., sampled, canary)
  - redact_version (string)  // which redaction rules applied to link to compliance logic

Why this flat shape?
- Avoids huge JSON blobs per request, plays well with log ingestion pipelines (BigQuery/ClickHouse) and can be partitioned by evaluation_ts and customer_id.
- Still allows reconstructing the evaluation ordering and basic numerical reasoning. Full replay is possible if we separately archive the policy_bundle snapshot referenced by policy_bundle_id.

Sampling, retention, and privacy
- Default: sample 1% of requests for full x-logs, sample 0.1% to include prompt hashes (for debug), store rest with more aggressive aggregation (only counts and errors).
- Retention: 90 days for sampled full x-logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics, 7 years for decision fingerprints required for enterprise audit on per-contract basis.
- PII: never include raw user text; include only prompt hash if permitted by customer. If a customer enables forensic-mode, require KMS-protected storage and explicit consent.

Performance and cost controls
- Budgeted evaluation: the evaluator runs with a CPU budget per request; if exceeded, we fall back to a cheaper scoring path (precomputed heuristics + last-known-good candidate).
- Fast-path: for many high-throughput routes we maintain pre-scored candidate lists with TTL (the score is only recalculated on bundle change or daily TTL expiry).
- Telemetry: headers on request include evaluation_time_ms and whether fast-path used. Those feed SLO dashboards.

Interplay with multi-region routing and control plane
- Policy bundle snapshots are versioned in the control plane and replicated to regional caches. Each evaluation records the snapshot id so the decision can be reproduced.
- Region-affinity: a light penalty applied during scoring for cross-region candidates; but penalty weight is configurable by customer: some enterprise customers prefer strict regional constraints (hard) rather than soft penalties.
- Failover behavior: when a regional capacity alarm triggers, control plane flips a region_ineligible hard-constraint in the active bundle. Evaluators pick that up within control-plane cache TTL (configurable; recommend < 10s for critical capacity signals).

Explainability use-cases and examples
- SRE incident: large spike in latency -> query x-logs for top candidates where latency_estimate_ms >> observed. Look for pattern: weight_vector skew toward older quantized variants.
- Customer question: why model X charged more? Use cost_estimate_usd in x-logs and the decision fingerprint to fetch the bundle and weights used.
- Audit: regulatory request for decisions in date range -> use decision fingerprints + sampled prompt hashes to assemble minimal evidence set (requires customer consent).

Operator debugging playbook (short)
1) Query recent evaluation_id for request_id.
2) Fetch x-log entries for that evaluation_id (all candidates).
3) Verify policy_bundle_id and fetch bundle snapshot from control plane store.
4) Re-run evaluator locally with same context and snapshot in a sandbox (replay tool will use same normalization seeds).
5) If discrepancy, check evaluator_version and the evaluator's fast-path flag.

Open design questions / TODOs
- Score explainability granularity: do we encode per-constraint provenance names or just index-aligned arrays? Index arrays are smaller but harder to decode without bundle metadata.
- Binary vs. graded constraints: do we architect a single uniform scorer or keep separate hard-constraint engine + soft-scorer? Current preference: hybrid (short-circuit hard, then graded).
- Cost of storing x-logs at scale: evaluate compressed columnar store vs. time-series with per-hour aggregation.
- Standardized provenance tags for cross-team correlation (e.g., experiment:billing-quantize-v2).

Appendix: example x-log entry (CSV-like flattened)
- evaluation_id=0f7a-... , request_id=r-3742 , customer_id=hash(abc123) , policy_bundle_id=bundle-2025-05-01-v12 , candidate_id=gptx-7b-q4f:us-west-2 , candidate_rank=1 , final_score=87.3 , hard_fail_reasons= , soft_scores=0.92,0.71,0.45 , weight_vector=0.5,0.3,0.2 , latency_estimate_ms=42.6 , cost_estimate_usd=0.0024 , cache_hit=false , short_circuit_stage=scoring , decision=accept , decision_ts=2025-07-02T15:12:09Z , evaluator_version=2025-06-18-rc3 , provenance_tags=sampled,canary , redact_version=v1

Notes for implementation owners
- Control-plane: ensure bundle snapshots are immutable and small; include explicit mapping of constraint id -> human label to decode soft_scores arrays.
- Serving runtime: expose hooks to attach cache_hit and kv-prefix stats to the decision context.
- Observability: add dashboard tiling for evaluation_time_ms by route and by policy_bundle_id.

Summary
A compact, index-aligned x-log plus an immutable bundle snapshot enables reproducible, low-cost explainability for the policy evaluation engine. Emphasize short-circuiting hard constraints to avoid unnecessary cost, sampling for privacy and storage control, and clear provenance (bundle id + evaluator version) to make replays reliable.

Action items
- [ ] Consensus on x-log field set and retention policy (owners: Maya, Rafael)
- [ ] Add bundle snapshot TTL and retrieval API in control plane (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Prototype compressed columnar storage for sampled x-logs (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Add runbook entry for forensic requests requiring KMS storage (security lead)
